hypothesis: Dated, locally available soybean-arrival forecasts versus stocks and planned crush may predict feedstock bottlenecks.
mechanism: A two-week feedstock balance changes feasible crushing before joint product replenishment.
counterexample: Vessels arrive but customs/quality clearance delays usability; processors cancel crush plans; demand falls faster than output.

mechanism: A margin-change signal is gated by raw availability and the tighter of distinct meal/oil inventory constraints.
counterexample: Margins reflect a meal/oil demand shock or unhedgeable quotes; maintenance, logistics or absent buyers prevent more crush.
